content.user_title: Diagnose Complex Bugs with a Reproducible Loop
content.value_statement: Hard bugs waste time when investigation starts without a reliable reproduction. This skill builds a tight feedback loop, tests hypotheses, and verifies durable fixes.
actual_capabilities: Builds a fast, deterministic pass-or-fail signal for a reported bug.
Guides reproduction minimization by removing one input, dependency, or step at a time.
Produces three to five ranked hypotheses with falsifiable predictions.
Maps targeted instrumentation to specific hypotheses and performance baselines.
Verifies fixes with regression tests, the original scenario, and cleanup checks.
limitations: Requires access to code, logs, tests, or an environment that can reproduce the symptom.
Cannot guarantee a deterministic loop for failures controlled by inaccessible external systems.
Does not replace domain knowledge when several causes produce the same observable result.
The human-in-the-loop template requires manual interaction for workflows that cannot be automated.

use_cases.title: Debug Application Failures
use_cases.description: Reproduce a difficult application failure, minimize the scenario, rank causes, and verify a focused fix.

use_cases.title: Trace Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Establish a performance baseline, bisect changes, and validate that the regression is removed.

use_cases.title: Create Durable Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Turn a reported defect into a deterministic regression test at the correct system boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Reproduce a Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this bug: [symptom]. First create and run the smallest reliable pass-or-fail loop. Show the command, result, and exact assertion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis of a clearly reported failure

prompt_templates.title: Minimize and Rank Causes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this failing reproduction: [command and output]. Minimize it one variable at a time. Then present three to five ranked, falsifiable hypotheses with predicted outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Performance Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this performance regression: [baseline and current behavior]. Build a repeatable benchmark, measure a baseline, bisect likely changes, and test one variable at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Diagnosis and Prevention
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [complex failure] using a deterministic feedback loop. Instrument only boundaries that separate ranked hypotheses. Produce the root cause, regression test, verified fix, cleanup evidence, and one prevention recommendation.

output_examples.input: A checkout action fails intermittently after a recent release.
output: Feedback loop: repeat the checkout scenario with fixed test data and record the exact payment error.
Minimized case: one discount code and one payment method reproduce the failure.
Leading cause: shared validation mutates the discount state before payment authorization.
Verification: the regression test passes, and the original checkout loop remains green across repeated runs.

output_examples.input: An API endpoint became slower after a dependency update.
output: Baseline: the repeatable request benchmark confirms a substantial latency increase.
Bisection: the first slow version introduces an additional remote lookup.
Fix: cache the stable lookup result within the request scope.
Verification: benchmark latency returns to baseline without changing response behavior.

best_practices: Create and run a red-capable feedback loop before forming detailed theories.
Change one variable at a time and connect every probe to a falsifiable prediction.
Re-run both the regression test and the original scenario before declaring completion.
anti_patterns: Do not read large areas of code before establishing a reliable reproduction.
Do not collect broad logs without a hypothesis that explains what each probe distinguishes.
Do not accept a passing shallow test when it does not exercise the real failure pattern.

faq.question: What does this skill diagnose?
faq.answer: It covers functional bugs, intermittent failures, incorrect output, thrown errors, and performance regressions.

faq.question: Can it apply a fix automatically?
faq.answer: It guides diagnosis and fix verification. Available tools and repository permissions determine which actions the agent can perform.

faq.question: Does it support intermittent bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It raises the reproduction rate through repetition, controlled stress, pinned randomness, and narrower timing conditions.

faq.question: How does it handle performance problems?
faq.answer: It establishes a repeatable baseline, uses profiling or query plans, bisects changes, and measures the result after each fix.

faq.question: Does it require an existing test suite?
faq.answer: No. It can use a failing test, command-line harness, browser script, captured trace, or structured human procedure.

faq.question: How does it determine that work is complete?
faq.answer: The original reproduction no longer fails, regression coverage passes, temporary instrumentation is removed, and the root cause is documented.
